rule.description: A named function frame (function, hook closure, or class method) is envious when it reaches, at least twice, directly into the declared data members of a project-declared data-owner instance that the frame does not belong to — reading, writing, or invoking the owner's fields from outside instead of asking the owning instance through one of its methods. Accesses inside inline anonymous callbacks count toward the named frame that defines them. Invoking a thin accessor of the owner (a getter or setter that only forwards to one of the owner's own data members) counts as a data touch, because the data stay with the caller and the reachability is unchanged; invoking a genuine method that performs the owner's work counts as proper delegation and is not a touch.
rule.detection: Two passes over the repository's own TypeScript sources under src/: pass 1 catalogs every project-declared class (its declared fields with annotated field types, its methods, which methods are thin accessors whose body is exactly `return this.x` or `this.x = v`, and its exported module-level singletons); pass 2 resolves, for every member access in every function frame, which cataloged owner instance the receiver denotes (via constructor calls, ref unwrapping, annotated parameters and fields, or imported singletons), and counts touches of declared data members with a foreign owner — direct touches, function-valued field invocations, and invocations of thin accessors alike. Threshold: two or more foreign data-member touches in one named frame.

checks.description: Detect named functions that keep data-owner behavior locally: they read, write, or invoke the declared data members of a cataloged owner instance directly instead of asking that owner through its methods.
checks.detected_relation: named function frame -> foreign data member of a cataloged data-owner instance
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The frame is more interested in the data of another owner than in its own; the behavior around that data belongs with the owner, so repeated direct touches of the owner's fields mark misplaced responsibility.

matches.evidence: The hook body resolves the default serializer functions from the shared store's fields (parseDefault at line 53, stringifyDefault at line 54) instead of asking the store, and re-keys the per-key storage holder by writing its key data member from outside (line 63).

The subscription callback adds the store-change listener to the cross-instance sync registry by inserting into and deleting from the registry's listener set data member directly (lines 72 and 73), instead of the registry managing its own subscription bookkeeping.

The snapshot callback consults the shared store's fallback map by calling data members of it (lines 81 and 82), reads the storage holder's cached parsed value (line 82), overwrites the holder's cached parsed value (lines 85, 87, and 97) and its cached raw string (lines 83 and 91) from outside the holder.

The state setter bases the next value on the holder's cached parsed value (line 108), invokes the shared store's storage-area resolver field from outside (line 117), and manages the store's in-memory fallback map by deleting from and inserting into that data member directly (lines 119 and 121).

The removal callback invokes the shared store's storage-area resolver field from outside (line 129) and mutates the store's in-memory fallback map data member directly (line 131) instead of letting the store own its removal bookkeeping.

The per-key holder's read operation invokes the shared store's storage-area resolver field from outside (line 39) and manages the store's in-memory fallback map by probing and inserting into that data member directly (lines 41 and 42).

The store's default-persistence operation works with the storage holder's data instead of its own: it reads the holder's stringify function-valued field (line 46) and the holder's default value (lines 46 and 49), writes through the holder's key (line 47), and sets the holder's cached raw string (line 48) and cached parsed value (line 49) from outside the holder.

excluded.reason: It touches a foreign owner's listener set only once per frame, below the relation's threshold of two distinct data-member touches; a single delegation-sized touch is treated as bookkeeping, not misplaced behavior.

excluded.reason: It reads only the browser event's own payload fields and the global storage area; neither the hook's data owners nor their declared data members participate.

excluded.reason: Its accesses to data members are assignments on its own instance; own-class touches are self-management, not envy.
